title: Thinstate KV-Bridge weekly sync
body:
Purpose and context:
This note captures the thinstate KV-bridge workstream updates from this week. Thinstate is our lightweight kernel shim idea to split KV cache lifecycle and batch scheduling from the heavy attention kernels so we can reduce tail latency for cold prefix hits and improve packing efficiency for short requests. The objective this sprint: validate viability on p4d replicas, measure 95/99p latency delta, and identify integration blockers for Dedicated pools.

Attendees:
- Claire Zhang (owner)
- David Morales (benchmarks)
- Rohan Mehta (kernel lead)
- Elena Koval (SRE)
- Maya Kim (product, observability)

Summary of what we did this week:
1) Prototype iteration (thinstate v0.3):
- Implemented separate lifecycle thread for thinstate that exposes a tiny RPC to the runtime for cache warm-up and eviction hints. This avoids a full kernel thread context switch when serving short, non-streaming requests.
- Added a compact header to requests that indicates whether prefix-cache can be reused (client-side opt-in).
- Hooked thinstate into the prefetch path so prefill requests trigger an early KV load with lower priority.

2) Benchmarks and initial numbers (p4d, sequence=64, mixed load):
- Baseline: current mainline runtime (no thinstate). 95p latency: 78ms; 99p latency: 240ms; median throughput: 340 qps
- thinstate v0.3 (opt-in): 95p latency: 52ms (-33%); 99p latency: 160ms (-33%); median throughput: 370 qps (+9%)
- Observed improved packing for short requests (avg tokens per request 18 => effective batch size increased by ~12%).
- Cold-start penalty for first KV fill: additional 8ms but subsequent requests benefit.

3) Observability changes:
- Added thinstate-specific spans and metrics: thinstate.acquire_ms, thinstate.prefetch_hit, thinstate.evict_count. Metrics are behind feature flag and sent to a separate metrics stream for now to avoid dashboard spam.
- Maya created a per-route burn-down view to correlate thinstate_prefetch_hit with token-level cost.

Key decisions and notes:
- Decision: Keep opt-in toggle for three more sprints while we validate behavior on Dedicated pools (risk: untested KMS interactions for Private).
- Decision: thinstate RPC should be bounded to 512 bytes payload and always keep a 2ms soft timeout in the scheduler to avoid blocking kernel hot paths.
- Note: For quantized kernels, we must ensure the thinstate eviction policy is aware of per-shard memory compaction; otherwise we can get subtle OOMs during heavy quantized model loads. Rohan will add a safety check in the allocator.

Risks and open questions:
- Backpressure interaction: if thinstate prefetch saturates the I/O path, it could increase latency for long-running streaming requests. Need to add adaptive rate limiter. (TODO: SERV-4321)
- Observability gap: 99p improvements are promising in our synthetic mix but we lack good production-like chat traces. Requesting Solutions Eng to seed a canary traffic pattern.
- Compatibility: Private deployments with air-gapped KMS may require a fallback path. This week discovered a failure mode where KMS key access latency >200ms caused thinstate RPC timeouts.

Action items (owner, eta):
- Rohan Mehta: Add allocator safety check for quantized shards (+ guardrail logging). ETA: 2026-07-29.
- David Morales: Run Dedicated-pool soak for 48h with thinstate opt-in flag; collect p95/p99 and memory churn. ETA: 2026-07-27.
- Elena Koval: Implement adaptive prefetch rate limiter prototype (leaky-bucket) and wire to scheduler. ETA: 2026-08-02.
- Maya Kim: Create a canary config and coordinate with Solutions Eng to route 2% of internal chat traffic through thinstate in staging. ETA: 2026-07-24.
- Claire Zhang: Draft rollout plan for Dedicated with rollback thresholds and update the rollout playbook. ETA: 2026-07-30.

Experimental observations and hypotheses to test next week:
- Hypothesis A: Increasing thinstate prefetch priority for short requests will further reduce p99 by ~10ms but risks throughput for bulk batches. Will A/B test three priority levels.
- Hypothesis B: A small LRU on the thinstate side (64k entries) yields a much higher prefetch hit rate for conversational workloads compared to pure prefix-only heuristics. Need trace-backed simulation.

Notes from kernel sync with Rohan:
- Kernel change K-1872 (prefill scheduling adjustment) landed in feature branch; initial integration with thinstate showed a rare race: if thinstate evicts a key while kernel still has an in-flight KV reference, we get a double-free in the allocator during heavy churn. Short-term mitigation: allocator reference counting. Long-term: borrow-free handoff protocol.
- Rohan estimates allocator refcount patch will add ~2% CPU cost but remove the crash. Prioritized for this sprint.

Customer/partner considerations:
- No external customers are currently using thinstate. Sales asked whether this can be toggled per-customer on Dedicated — answer: yes, and we'll include per-customer toggle in rollout plan.
- Compliance: Private deployments with strict audit trails require thinstate RPC logs to be persisted to the audit store; adding log hooks will be an opt-in enterprise feature.

Meeting decisions for next sync:
- Continue opt-in experiments; next sync will present Dedicated soak report (David).
- If allocator refcount patch stabilizes, run a stress test with quantized models.
- Prepare short executive one-pager describing thinstate benefit for product/ops (Claire + Maya).

Misc notes / scratch reminders:
- Check interactions with token-caching in the Console (console route proxies may disable the compact header).
- Run eviction policy simulation offline using replay traces from 2026-06 traffic.
- Add unit test for thinstate RPC timeout behavior (2ms boundary).

Attachments / quick links:
- Perf diff script: tools/perf/bench_thinstate.sh (WIP)
- Local reproduce: docker-compose-thinstate.yaml in repo root
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/982

If anything is missing or you want a deeper breakdown of the p99 distribution by model family, call out here and David will add the per-model CSVs to the next update.

-- Claire
